ai.summary: A Reuters investigation reports that a hacker used AI agents to probe and breach websites at more than 100 companies, with the agents performing much of the work autonomously. Researchers said the activity demonstrates how readily available agent tools could make complex cyberattacks easier for individual criminals.
ai.title: How one hacker used AI agents and a few thousand dollars to break into scores of sites

ai.summary: Anthropic said it plans to place 5% of its shares in a new public-benefit fund, subject to shareholder approval, with the possibility of adding shares as the company’s valuation rises. The fund could support nonprofit donations or direct aid, including efforts related to AI’s labor-market impact; its governance and detailed structure are still to come.
ai.title: Anthropic to commit 5% stake to new 'public benefit fund'

ai.summary: Eight U.S. states are suing OpenAI, alleging that ChatGPT has caused consumer harms, including dangerous advice and risks to children. OpenAI says it has built safety protections for children and will continue improving them.
ai.title: States sue AI giant OpenAI, saying its popular chatbot is hurting children and deceiving adults

ai.summary: Microsoft withdrew from a reported agreement with data-center developer Nscale at Loughton, where grid power was reportedly not expected until the 2030s. Nscale said other Microsoft contracts were unaffected and that it was exploring alternative power arrangements.
ai.title: Microsoft withdraws from Nscale Loughton data-center agreement

quantum.summary: Quantinuum reported 99.9995% logical memory fidelity on its Helios-1 trapped-ion system using a color code—about five uncorrectable errors per million operations. Logical memory errors fell roughly 12-fold with each tested increase in code size, although error rates were higher for logical operations than for memory.
quantum.title: Error-correction record pushes quantum computers closer to usefulness

quantum.summary: Google researchers demonstrated magic-state cultivation on its Willow processor, reporting 99.99% logical fidelity and about a 40-fold reduction in errors for these states. The technique addresses a key resource for fault-tolerant computation, but still needs to be scaled before it can underpin practical machines.
quantum.title: Google demonstrates method to cut errors in quantum computing’s ‘magic states’

quantum.summary: Researchers led by the University of Edinburgh reported an algorithm that reduces the computing resources needed for classical simulations of photonic quantum devices to about 5% of the previous requirement. In Gaussian boson sampling tests, the simulations matched or outperformed some current devices, potentially helping researchers evaluate and design photonic systems.
quantum.title: Advance Could Lead to Bigger, More Reliable Quantum Computers, University of Edinburgh Scientists Say

quantum.summary: RIKEN researchers demonstrated parallel control of silicon spin qubits in a five-qubit array using a shared microwave line. Their calibration method maintained gate fidelities above 99.99% for up to three simultaneously operated qubits and about 99.9% across all five, addressing a challenge for scaling control.
quantum.title: RIKEN Team Improves Parallel Control of Silicon Spin Qubits

quantum.summary: Photonic quantum-computing company Xanadu said DARPA provisionally approved up to $10 million in additional funding through its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative. The one-year extension is intended to support R&D toward fault-tolerant, utility-scale photonic computing; the announcement is a company statement, not an independent assessment of progress.
quantum.title: Xanadu Secures Up to USD $10 Million in Additional DARPA Support to Accelerate Quantum R&D Roadmap

quantum.summary: Chinese startup Tuoyuan is pursuing neutral-atom quantum computing and has reportedly set a goal of 100 logical qubits. The financing details cited in the report have not been independently verified, and the company has not disclosed hardware benchmarks or a delivery timeline.
quantum.title: China’s Tuoyuan Targets Neutral-Atom Quantum Computing
